title: Canonical shifts of scalar proper/open mates and scalar limit maps
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], with algebraic closure $k$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E\subset F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $A=\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_F$, $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_F$ and $e\geq1$ with $tB=v^eB$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_c}Y)$ with $j$ open and $p_c$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $C_W=-\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, the derived-complete bounded constructible category with a uniform Tor-amplitude interval for all reductions [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $A_n=A/t^n$, $B_n=B/t^nB=B/v^{en}$, $M_n=M\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$, and $C_W^{(n)}=-\otimes^L_{(A_n)_W}(B_n)_W$. For $H=E,F$, let $P_H^c$ be the integral compact-support functor attached to $c$, defined as the total derived inverse limit of its finite separately derived proper/open images [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

Use the strict reduction lifts $\mathcal T_E^c(M)$ and $\mathcal T_F^c(C_XM)$ of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor], restricted to the discrete constant ring sheaves $\underline A$ and $\underline B$. A strict tower means a complex in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_W))$ or its $B$ analogue, with its ordinary derived category [def-weil-inverse-system, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A superscript $(e)$ retains indices $en$ with composite transitions. Put $T=-\otimes_A B$ on constant-coefficient tower complexes; all finite coefficient objects are regarded as constant integral modules by restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

Use the proper/open scalar mate $q_\bullet^c$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate]. Give derived scalar extension, inverse image and separately derived direct image their canonical integer-shift comparisons, and give exact extension by zero its degreewise shift comparison [def-weil-triangulated-category]. On both the original ringed sites and the small ringed diagram sites, the proper scalar mate commutes with these shifts: its transpose at $N[1]$, after the canonical identifications, is $(C\varepsilon_N)[1]$. The open tensor map also commutes with shift, with the same sign on the shifted differential. Thus $q_\bullet^c(M[1])$ is the shifted $q_\bullet^c(M)$ under the specified source and target comparisons, as a strict-tower equality before taking limits.

Normalize the scalar shift maps by the universal derived-scalar counit, regarded as a right Kan extension of the complex-level scalar functor through the localization to the derived category: the shift comparisons are the unique ones making that counit commute with shift, and they obey the coherent integer-shift laws. Under total derived limit and the exact compact-support tower shifts, the above strict equation is the corresponding equation for the total-limit mate.

On a K-flat representative the ordinary/completed strict scalar comparison $\chi_{F/E,N}$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] is the compatible quotient product map with zero shifted-product component in the Roos cone. It commutes with the specified shifts, including the cone sign. Consequently for the map $\gamma_M=r_e^{-1}\mathsf R(q_\bullet^c)\tau$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-scalar-limit-reduction] one has $s_{P_F^cC_X}\gamma_{M[1]}=\gamma_M[1]s_{C_YP_E^c}$, where each $s$ is the canonical shift comparison of that composite. The equality and its coherent iterates concern the actual ordinary-tensor and strict-tower comparison maps.

proof.text: Use the unchanged canonical shift structures and OriginalMateShift predicate from [def-pur-compact-support-scalar-shift-structures]. Original-site mate compatibility is [lem-pur-original-scalar-mate-shift]. The diagram constituents and strict arrow commute with shifts by [lem-pur-strict-scalar-mate-shift].

Completed and finite scalar counit normalization is the already proved helper [lem-pur-scalar-counit-shift-unique]. For ordinary tensor localization, take its canonical shift. Two shifts making mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom commute yield the same component square. Cancel the invertible localization shift and the invertible factor map, and use localization natural-transformation extensionality. Structure extensionality identifies the two CommShift structures.

Apply [lem-pur-scalar-limit-constraint-shift] for the completion, tensor/limit and forward restriction constraints, and the total-limit component equation for the actual scalarLimitArrow. The latter is the whiskered strict arrow composed with tensor/limit and inverse arithmetic restriction, with canonical associators.

Use [lem-pur-compact-support-scalar-shift-witness] for the exact normalized scalar witness gamma, its factorization and its shift square. The strict-arrow square of the final clause is the component form of the arrow CommShift of [lem-pur-strict-scalar-mate-shift], and the scalarLimitArrow square is the last clause of [lem-pur-scalar-limit-constraint-shift]. Combine these with the constituent squares and the two independently proved normalization uniqueness arguments by conjunction introduction.
